PASS otherwise; informational cells are reported as reach / noReach / unexplained

claimLimits.label: H, consistent with B-layers and B-release
text: X8 shows blocking of the counted channels only; an uncounted channel toward another destination is not covered.
Destination independence rests on CSP, DNR and RtcLockdown not distinguishing destinations except the chrome-extension exception; this is an argument, not a proof.
RtcLockdown's argument remains unproven (B); a passing X8 does not prove WebRTC exposure is impossible.

precisionBlocks.text: UDP 19000 has no channel in any source: it is a listener only; any event on it counts as reach in its window.
C7's transport is not fixed (H34: 'RTCPeerConnection from the new realm'); the fixture reuses C5's STUN configuration.
K2's relaxed CSP is described ('allows the canary') but not written; the fixture text is a proposal.
What remains when the CSP layer is off is not written; the fixture keeps the sandbox token only.
RtcLockdown's mechanism is not defined in the current baseline; X8 tests its effect, not its design.
Whether document.write (C7 path 5) can create a realm under the blob-script loader is undefined; the K4 control decides testability.
TCP 18443 is named 'WebSocket'; TLS is not specified. The fixture uses ws:// because reach is measured at TCP accept.
STUN/TURN traffic carries no path; attribution uses one page per time window (schedule P).
DNR rule fields beyond id, priority and urlFilter (action, condition.tabIds) are not written.
Chrome may refuse private-network destinations; then K4 shows 'untestable' and the canary must move (second machine or public address), as H34 and B-canaryLocal allow.
The secondary monitor and X8-full come from H34 only; the current baseline names CanarySink alone.
The extension-API probe is informational here; the gate for extension APIs is X4.
